## Rule

ARC-GEN `f8c80d96`: size 10. Input shows the first 2 or 3 nested square frames in one non-gray color on black. Output has gray (5) background and completes every same-color frame to the 10x10 edge. The frame center is on the top edge `(0, col)` or left edge `(row, 0)`. `thick` is 1 or 2, with frame radius period `thick + 1`.

## Algorithm sketch

Decode the visible color, edge center, and `thick` from the shown frames; emit color where the generated square-frame predicate holds and gray elsewhere. The current canonical graph does not do this decode; it nearest-template matches a 10x10 crop to 76 prototypes, looks up a 10-row bit code, expands it to a 10x10 mask, then colorizes from `ReduceMax(input)`.

## Cost analysis

Original cost 50,534 (memory=47,852, params=2,682) dominated by eight [1,1,30,30] Mul intermediates (v69-v76, 8×3,600=28,800B) plus their Concat antecedents (v55,v56,v58,v59 = 2×1200+2×3600=9,600B). v7[1,1,30,30], v8[1,1,10,20], v9[1,1,20,30] initializers are all zeros (1,700 params, 6,800B). Since padding is zero, the 30×30 Concats just zero-pad 10×10 computed tensors. Restructuring defers padding to a single final Pad→'output' (excluded from scoring), computing channels at 10×10 scale instead. Result: cost 18,034 (memory=17,052, params=982).

2026-06-19 ringgen floor note: a non-lookup rule rebuild must still write a 10-channel 30x30 one-hot with gray background. The only credible sub-1009 family is a direct final-output Conv: area <= 9 with bias costs <=910, or area 10 without bias costs 1000. The task-local audit hashes official input patches and proves every such rectangular support has identical patches with different required outputs (best case among audited supports: 2x5 no-bias still has 3244 conflicts). Equal-tail/canvas routes start at 900-1000 bytes for the required canvas/one-hot surface before center/thickness/color decode, leaving no room to beat 1009.

2026-06-24 current candidate: cost 1001 (memory 770, params 231), a strict −8 versus run team-best 1009. Dominant charged tensors remain the unpack/render tail: `bit_and [1,1,10,10] U16` 200 B, `sign10_h [1,1,10,10] F16` 200 B, `B10_bool [1,1,10,10]` 100 B, and `hash_cells_f32 [1,21]` 84 B. The improvement is formulation-local, not a new rule route: it removes one redundant hash probe and rebuilds the packed row tables for the resulting signed indices.
